title: Chapter 2 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of HTML elements, attributes, nesting, void tags, and semantics!

questions.question: Which part of an HTML element contains the content?
options: Between the opening and closing tags
questions.explanation:
Content lives between the opening and closing tags (e.g., `

content

`).

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for an attribute?
questions.explanation: Attributes follow `name="value"` format, always within the opening tag.

questions.question: The `id` attribute can be used multiple times on the same page.
questions.explanation: `id` values must be unique – one per element.

questions.question: Which attribute is used to group multiple elements for styling?
questions.explanation: `class` is designed for grouping; multiple elements can share the same class.

questions.question: What does the `title` attribute typically do?
questions.explanation: The `title` attribute provides advisory information, often displayed as a tooltip.

questions.question: Which of the following is correctly nested?
questions.explanation: Tags must close in the reverse order they were opened.

questions.question: Self‑closing tags like `` require a closing tag in HTML5.
questions.explanation: HTML5 void elements are written simply as `` without a closing tag.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a void element?
questions.explanation: is a normal element that requires a closing tag.

questions.question: Block‑level elements by default:
options: Only take up as much width as necessary
Start on a new line and stretch full width
questions.explanation: Block elements begin on a new line and take the full available width.

questions.question: Which element is inline by default?
questions.explanation: <span> is a generic inline container; the others are block.

questions.question: You can place a block element inside an inline element.
questions.explanation: Inline elements cannot contain block elements; it violates HTML rules.

questions.question: What is the purpose of semantic HTML?
options: To make the code run faster
To give meaning to the structure, aiding accessibility and SEO
questions.explanation: Semantic tags describe the role of content, improving accessibility and search engine understanding.

questions.question: Which tag is appropriate for a blog post title within an article?
questions.explanation: A heading tag (`<h2>` etc.) should be used for titles, providing document outline structure.

questions.question: The ______ attribute provides a unique identifier for a single element.
questions.explanation: The `id` attribute uniquely identifies one element on the page.

questions.question: How should you separate multiple class names?
questions.explanation: Multiple classes are separated by spaces, e.g., `class="btn primary"`.

questions.question: Comments can be placed anywhere in the HTML document.
questions.explanation: HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) can appear almost anywhere, even inside head or body.

questions.question: Which element would you use for the main navigation links?
questions.explanation: <nav> is the semantic element for navigation blocks.

questions.question: What is the `<main>` element used for?
options: The dominant content of the document, unique to the page
questions.explanation: <main> represents the primary content area, and there should be only one per page.

questions.question: A `<div>` has no semantic meaning.
questions.explanation: <div> is a pure container with no inherent meaning; it's used for styling or grouping when no semantic tag fits.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly uses the `lang` attribute?
questions.explanation: The correct attribute is `lang` applied to the `<html>` tag (or any element) to specify language.

questions.question: What is the purpose of indentation in HTML?
options: Changes the layout of the page
questions.explanation: Indentation is for developer readability; browsers ignore it.

questions.question: The `<head>` element is displayed on the page.
questions.explanation: Content inside `<head>` (except `<title>`) is not rendered visually; it's metadata.

questions.question: Which tag is used to emphasise text, typically rendering it italic?
questions.explanation: <em> emphasises text and browsers often render it italic. <strong> indicates strong importance (bold).

questions.question: A child element is one that:
options: Is written on the same line
Is nested directly inside another element
questions.explanation: A child element is directly inside a parent element in the DOM tree.
